result.output:
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint hit from another GitHub repo, add --repo <owner/name> to
'entire checkpoint explain' (requires the full checkpoint ID; unrelated to
this command's --repo filter below).

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Usage:
  entire search [query] [flags]

Examples:
  entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

Flags:
      --all-repos        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string    Filter by author name
      --branch string    Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code             Search code content across repositories
      --compact          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string      Filter by time period (week or month)
  -h, --help             help for search
      --json             Output as JSON
      --limit int        Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int         Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings     Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
=== CHECKPOINT ===
Operations on checkpoints — the persistent records of agent work tied to commits.

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint tokens <id>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"

Usage:
  entire checkpoint [command]

Aliases:
  checkpoint, cp, checkpoints

Available Commands:
  explain     Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
  list        List checkpoints on the current branch
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  tokens      Show token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for checkpoint

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Use "entire checkpoint [command] --help" for more information about a command.
=== EXPLAIN ===
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

Usage:
  entire checkpoint explain [checkpoint-id | commit-sha] [flags]

content.text:
Good news: your index is rich and the drill-down works. One gotcha first, then the queries I verified.

## Run the demo from `tedlasso-strava/`, not the 2.0 parent

This is the thing that would bite you on stage. From the parent repo, `entire search` returns great hits, but every drill-down fails:

```
$ entire checkpoint explain 07d55332ee9e84eec4b36c642c --short
no checkpoint or commit found matching "07d55332..."
```

The hits belong to `elizabethsiegle/tedlasso-strava`, the nested repo. `cd tedlasso-strava` first and the exact same command resolves. Also note only the two checkpoints on `feat/route-basemap` resolve locally; main-branch commits like `4515e5cf` hit `checkpoint not found: 01M04D4F1FDB...` because that checkpoint hasn't been fetched. Stay on the current branch's checkpoints.

## Tier 1: the search-to-explain money shot

These score 40+ and return a **session hit paired with its commit**, and `explain` resolves cleanly:

```bash
entire search "overlay the route on a city street map"      # session 51.5 + commit 69121be
entire search "timezone handling for late night runs"       # session 42.1 + commit 07d5533
entire search "proxy map tiles through the worker"          # 36.9
```

Then drill in. The commit sha straight from the search result works as the argument:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain 69121be
```

That prints the intent (`"could you make the map also include the map of the city?"`), all 15 touched files, and the full transcript with every tool call the agent made. That is the part people have not seen before.

## Tier 2: proving it isn't grep

Queries with near-zero literal overlap that still land on the right session. Worth doing one of these right after a Tier 1, because it kills the "so it's just search" objection:

```bash
entire search "why does the run say yesterday"              # 18.8, nails the tz fix
entire search "making the UI not look AI generated"         # 15.1, hits the superpowers build session
entire search "what did the agent do when the API returned garbage"   # sessions only, 13.5
```

`"why does the run say yesterday"` is my pick for the single best line in the demo. It is how a human actually reports a bug, nobody wrote those words anywhere, and it returns exactly one session and one commit. No noise to explain away.

## On your `"cold path failover tests"` example

It works, but it is the weakest of the bunch for this demo: one commit hit, no session. Same for `"KV outage failover"` (2 commits) and `"rate limit 429 backoff"` (zero hits, avoid that one). Your infra-flavored phrasing pulls commits; the map and timezone work is where the *sessions* are indexed.

## Two prep items before you present

Both `explain` outputs currently say `Summary: Not generated yet`. That is a dead spot in an otherwise strong screen. Want me to run these so the AI summaries are populated?

```bash
entire checkpoint explain --generate 01M0G0WDKY2G7V3Z43SD3J221C
entire checkpoint explain --generate 01M0G7EEY07NRATRPTVEZF8EQ7
```

Also worth a mention if you have time: bare `entire search` opens an interactive table, `--compact` is the agent-facing shape, and inline filters (`author:lizzie`, `date:week`, `repo:*`) work in the query string itself.

content.text:
Diagnosed both halves. Here's what's actually going on.

## Checkpoints *are* being searched, they're just not labeled as such

Nothing is missing from the index. I searched the text of checkpoint `01M0G0WDKY...`'s own intent (`"could you make the map also include the map of the city"`), which appears nowhere in the commit message `feat: draw the route over a proxied street basemap`:

```
counts: {'checkpoints': 1, 'sessions': 1, 'commits': 0}
  commit   17.91  69121be7ddf40ad...  feat: draw the route over a proxied stre
  session  17.91  6d3b3863-c889-4b...  commit
```

`counts.checkpoints: 1` means a checkpoint matched. The identical 17.91 on both rows means that is one record surfaced twice, as its commit and its session. Across a 30-result sweep, zero result ids were checkpoint ULIDs. So a checkpoint tied to a commit always renders as the commit row, and you reach it with `explain`. That's a labeling gap in the results table, not absent data.

## But this repo's checkpoints genuinely aren't indexed

This is the bigger problem:

| | parent `tedlasso-strava2.0` | nested `tedlasso-strava/` |
|---|---|---|
| local checkpoint refs | **5** | 2 |
| on origin | **0** | 2 |
| upstream for `main` | none configured | tracked, in sync |
| shared history with origin | **none** | yes |

Both point at the same remote (`gh/elizabethsiegle/tedlasso-strava`), but the parent shares no commits with it and `main` has no upstream, so its 5 checkpoints have never shipped. That includes the good one, `01M0B7KR4RZQD8A8SMVH9VBET3` "Add implementation plan for Ted Lasso Strava mood board", plus a large `[temporary]` one spanning ~45 commits. Every hit in my earlier searches came from the nested repo. Pushing parent `main` there would be an unrelated-histories push, so I did not.

## The good news for making one right now

Your current session is registered in **both** worktrees, and in the nested repo it reads:

```
Worktree: tedlasso-strava   Status: active   Checkpoints: 0
Last prompt: "amazing now i really need a checkpoint..."
```

The nested repo is correctly wired and its checkpoints demonstrably push and index. It also has four uncommitted tooling files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.entire/settings.json`, `.entire/.gitignore`), and that repo already has precedent for exactly this commit (`1f0f1a72 chore: enable Entire tracking`). So a commit there produces a real checkpoint attached to this session, and a push makes it searchable.

That last step touches your remote, so I want your call before I do it.

[Assistant] Real bug, now fixed and committed as `07d5533`.

**What was wrong:** `facts.daysSinceLast` is elapsed time, and `agoLabel` called anything under 24 hours "today". Your 21:44 PDT ride was 0.57 days old at 11:32, so it read as today, and would have kept saying today until 21:44 that night. A UTC calendar check wouldn't have saved it either, since 21:44 PDT is 04:44 UTC the *next* day. The comparison has to happen in your `TIMEZONE`.

**The fix**, one helper rather than the math copy-pasted twice:

Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.237/624f5abe0f81ca2b8c2c01a9b96f979b/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

result.output:
# tedlasso-strava

A single-athlete Cloudflare Worker that reads my Strava activity every 4 hours, derives a
"mood" from it, and serves one Ted Lasso quote + GIF that matches.

## UI must not look AI-generated

The global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` rule applies here in full — read it, it lists the specific
tells that are banned. This section pins down what we do *instead* on this project, so nobody
has to re-litigate the aesthetic every session.

**The aesthetic is a non-league matchday programme.** Newsprint stock, heavy condensed
display type over a plain workhorse text face, a single ink accent per mood, hairline rules
doing the layout work instead of card shadows, stats set like a results table. Think a
printed team sheet someone folded into their back pocket — not a SaaS dashboard.

Concretely, on this project:
- No cards with shadows. Structure comes from rules, spacing, and type weight.
- The quote is the largest thing on the page by a wide margin. It is the design.
- Stats are set as a dense tabular block with tabular-lining numerals — deliberately tighter
  than the hero, because that density contrast is the whole layout.
- One accent color per mood, defined in the mood catalogue, used sparingly (rules, the mood
  label, the GIF border). The rest stays near-monochrome ink on stock.
- Off-grid human details are wanted: a rotated "MATCHDAY" stamp, a printer's registration
  mark, a slightly-too-tight kerned mood name.
- Server-rendered HTML with inline CSS. No component framework, no CSS framework, so there
  are no defaults to accidentally ship.

## Architecture

- Hexagonal layering: `src/domain` imports nothing from `src/infrastructure` — no I/O, no
  network, no Workers types, no React. Infrastructure implements interfaces the domain
  declares, never the reverse.
- Inject the clock. `now` is always a parameter in domain code; never call `Date.now()` or
  `new Date()` inside `src/domain`, so "9 days since your last run" is testable without
  waiting nine days.
- No `Math.random()` in the domain. Quote and GIF selection are seeded from the snapshot's
  `refreshedAt`, so output is a pure function of its inputs and tests assert exact strings.
- The mood engine is the safety-critical code here: fixture-based tests are ground truth. If
  the implementation and a fixture disagree, the implementation is wrong. Keep it at or near
  100% branch coverage.

## Domain constraints

- No scraping. All activity data comes from the official Strava API with my own OAuth token.
- One human click, ever: the initial Strava authorization. Everything after that — token
  rotation, refresh, scheduling — is automatic. Never design a flow that needs me to paste a
  token or run `wrangler secret put` as routine maintenance.
- The refresh token rotates on every use. Always persist the new one *before* using the
  access token it came with. A failed refresh must never clear the last good snapshot.
- The read path (page views) never calls Strava. It reads the KV snapshot only. Only the
  cron and the guarded manual-refresh endpoint may call Strava.
- Every mood, quote, and GIF lives in the versioned catalogue in `src/data/moods.ts` with a
  `verifiedOn` date — never hardcoded in rendering or engine logic. Flag GIF links whose
  `verifiedOn` is older than 180 days as stale.
- Never claim a "personal record." We only have 90 days of activity list data, so the honest
  claim is "longest ride in 90 days." Say what we can actually back.
- The route is drawn over a real basemap, and every tile is proxied through our own
  `/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` (`src/app/tiles.ts`). The browser must never request a tile from
  the upstream host directly: one Worker talking to the tile provider leaks nothing about
  visitors, a thousand browsers doing it leaks all of them. Basemap credit for OpenStreetMap
  and CARTO is rendered on the page, as their terms require.
- Two route path strings exist and are never interchangeable: `RouteRender.pathD` is
  equirectangular, normalised into an abstract 1000x1000 box, and `basemap.pathD` is Web
  Mercator in tile pixels. Mixing them draws the route over the wrong streets.
- Route polylines are privacy-trimmed at both ends in the *write* path, before anything is
  persisted. The snapshot stores finished SVG path data, never raw coordinates. We request
  `activity:read_all`, which bypasses Strava privacy zones, so an untrimmed route would
  publish a home address more precisely than the athlete's own Strava profile does. Never
  move trimming to render time, and never persist untrimmed coordinates "just in case."
  The basemap is built from the *redacted* segments, so it frames only geometry that was
  already cleared for publication. It does change what the published part reveals, though: a
  shape on paper is anonymous, and the same shape over a street map is an address. If that
  trade is ever unwanted, `BASEMAP=off` drops the tiles and keeps the route.
- Display "Powered by Strava" attribution with a link back, per Strava's brand guidelines.

result.output: ## 10. Decisions taken, with the reasoning - **Cron-and-snapshot over lazy revalidation.** Lazy refresh lets data rot when nobody visits, races between concurrent visitors, and makes page uptime depend on Strava's. - **KV over a Durable Object.** A DO would serialize token writes, but there is exactly one writer, so KV's consistency model is not a problem worth new infrastructure. - **Curated GIF list over a GIF API.** No API key, no rate limit, no second failure mode, and no off-topic results. Variety is bounded by curation, which is an acceptable trade. - **Overrides before the grid.** A pure grid cannot express "gone for ten days" or "just set a 90-day best", which are the most interesting states. A pure rule ladder loses the nuance of ordinary weeks. Both together cover both. - **No seed-token secret.** Its only job was bootstrap, which `/auth/login` now does better. Recovery becomes one click instead of a terminal session. - **No OAuth callback for visitors.** Single-athlete by design; the callback exists only for the owner and is gated twice. - **Inline SVG route over a tile-provider map.** The polyline is already in the data we fetch, so drawing it ourselves costs nothing: no API key, no per-view request to a third party, no client-side JavaScript, and no visitor data leaking to a tile host. It is also fully unit-testable as a pure function, and looks far less generic than an embedded map, which the project's UI rules require. **Revised 2026-08-20: the basemap is back, on our own terms.** A bare path reads as a shape with no place attached, and knowing *where* you ran is most of the point. What the original decision was actually protecting is preserved rather than traded away: - No API key and no client-side JavaScript: still true. `src/domain/basemap.ts` does the Web Mercator tile arithmetic server-side and emits a plain grid of `` elements plus one overlay `

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib

# ---- spec decision log ----
p = pathlib.Path("docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-tedlasso-strava-design.md")
s = p.read_text()
anchor = "- **Ghost trails deferred.**"
entry = """- **A weekly form guide, one measure on one axis.** Added 2026-08-20. The receipts could
  already say "4 this week vs your usual 2.5" but not whether that was a spike, a plateau or
  a recovery. Twelve weekly columns under the map answer it at a glance.

  - **Hours, not sessions and not distance.** One measure means one y-axis. A dual-scale
    figure (hours as columns, distance as a line) is the quickest way to make two unrelated
    numbers look correlated. Session count and distance ride along in each column's hover
    title and in the table beneath the figure, where they cannot be misread as a second
    scale.
  - **Ink columns, accent rule.** The accent budget on this project is rules, the mood label
    and the GIF border. Twelve accent columns would spend all of it on one figure, so the
    ink carries the data and the accent carries the single line it is measured against.
  - **Rest weeks count toward the median.** Dropping them would lift "usual" to a number the
    athlete never actually held. A zero week prints as a stub sitting on the rule rather than
    as an absent column, so it reads as nothing rather than as missing data.
  - **Its own week count.** `WORKLOAD_WEEKS` is deliberately separate from `BASELINE_WEEKS`:
    retuning the mood engine's baseline should not silently redraw the chart.
  - **Rolling 7-day buckets anchored to the athlete's today**, the same convention
    `computeBaseline` already uses, so "this week" means the same thing in the figure as in
    the receipts row directly above it.
  - **The median label sits at the left, in front of the columns.** It was right-aligned
    first, which printed it straight through this week's value label. The rule paints behind
    the columns so it never slices one, and the label paints in front of them over a stock
    white-out, the same trick the scale bar uses to stay legible over the map.
- **Plate furniture on the map.** Added 2026-08-20. Four printer's registration marks (which
  the UI rules ask for by name), a north arrow to go with the scale bar, and terminals on the
  route: a filled stud where the line starts, an open ring where it ends. The terminals mark
  the ends of the *trimmed* geometry, so they add direction to the figure without publishing a
  metre more than the path already draws. A loop lands both on the same point and the ring
  wins, which is the honest reading of a route that came back to where it started.
"""
assert anchor in s
p.write_text(s.replace(anchor, entry + anchor, 1))

# ---- CLAUDE.md domain constraints ----
p = pathlib.Path("CLAUDE.md")
s = p.read_text()
anchor = '- Display "Powered by Strava" attribution with a link back, per Strava\'s brand guidelines.'
entry = """- The form guide under the map is one measure on one axis: weekly moving time, in hours.
  Never give it a second y-scale. Session count and distance belong in the column hover
  titles and the table beneath the figure, never as a second series. The columns are ink and
  the median rule is the accent, not the other way round, and rest weeks are counted in the
  median so "usual" stays a number the athlete actually held.
- `Snapshot.workload`, `BasemapRender.start` and `BasemapRender.end` are optional, not merely
  nullable. Snapshots written before each of them exist in KV, and the read path has to
  survive being handed one, so guard on the key rather than trusting the type.
"""
assert anchor in s
p.write_text(s.replace(anchor, entry + anchor, 1))
print("docs updated")
PYEOF

## Intent

Improve an unsatisfactory checkpoint by making the map visualization prettier and adding a workout/activity chart with recent workout data beneath it, then commit a proper checkpoint.

## Outcome

Added a weekly workload domain module, extended the snapshot schema and write path, added start/end route terminals to the basemap, built a 'form guide' chart and map plate styling in render.ts, wrote and fixed unit/integration tests (426 passing, coverage above gate), visually verified light and dark renders via headless Chrome screenshots (catching and fixing a label collision bug), updated decision docs, and committed the feature.

## Learnings

### Repository

- Design system is a 'newsprint/matchday programme' aesthetic using --stock/--ink/--ink-accent CSS tokens with Georgia serif + uppercase letterspaced sans.
- The project follows a graph-first workflow (dataviz skill, graph search) before implementing chart/render features.
- Snapshot schema previously had no activity/workout time series — had to be added from scratch (types.ts, refresh.ts write path).
- Repo maintains a spec decision log (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-tedlasso-strava-design.md) and CLAUDE.md that should be updated when making design decisions.
- Repo has a standing rule against em dashes in code/comments, which the assistant violated inadvertently and had to strip out.
- Test fixtures/snapshots can predate new optional fields (e.g. basemap terminals), so new fields must be made optional for backward compatibility.

### Code

- `src/domain/basemap.ts` — Basemap module needed start/end route endpoints added as optional fields so older snapshots without them remain valid; used to show route direction on the map.
- `src/domain/tuning.ts` — Tuning constants file holds config values like WORKLOAD_WEEKS controlling how many weeks of workout data are bucketed.
- `src/app/render.ts` — Render layer builds both map plate furniture and the new form-guide chart; SVG rects needed a distinguishing class (form-bar) so test assertions could target actual bar elements instead of matching all rects (including a white-out background rect).

### Workflow

- Establishing a green baseline test run before making changes helps confirm which failures are caused by new work.
- Searching for existing 'strict shape assertion' tests before extending schemas helps avoid breaking exact-match tests unintentionally.
- Rendering an actual preview via esbuild bundling + headless Chrome screenshots (both light and dark themes) surfaced a real visual bug (label collision) that pure unit tests would have missed.
- Headless Chrome can reuse an existing instance/profile causing identical screenshots across theme variants — isolating Chrome profiles per screenshot run fixes this.
- After a visual fix, add a regression test (not just fix and move on) to pin the corrected behavior in the test suite.

content.text:
Done, and this one has real work in it.

## What I built

**A form guide under the map.** Twelve weekly columns of training volume, with the athlete's median week ruled across in the mood accent. New domain module `src/domain/workload.ts:47` derives the buckets as rolling 7-day windows anchored to the athlete's today, the same convention `computeBaseline` already uses, so "this week" means the same thing in the chart as in the receipts row directly above it.

Design calls worth naming, since you asked for prettier and not just more:

- **Ink columns, accent rule.** Your `CLAUDE.md` keeps the accent for rules, the mood label and the GIF border. Twelve accent columns would have spent that whole budget on one figure, so the ink carries the data and the accent carries the one line you measure it against.
- **One measure, one axis: hours.** Session count and distance ride along in each column's hover title and in a table beneath the figure, never as a second y-scale.
- **Rest weeks count toward the median**, and print as a stub sitting on the rule rather than an absent column, so a week off reads as nothing rather than as missing data.
- `WORKLOAD_WEEKS` is deliberately separate from `BASELINE_WEEKS` so retuning the mood engine doesn't silently redraw the chart.

**On the map:** four printer's registration marks (your UI rules ask for those by name), a north arrow to pair with the scale bar, and terminals on the route, a filled stud for the off and an open ring for the finish. Those mark the ends of the *trimmed* geometry, so they add direction without publishing a metre more than the path already draws. A loop lands both on the same point and the ring wins.

## The bug that only showed up when I looked at it

Tests were green and the chart was still wrong. I bundled the page with esbuild and screenshotted it in headless Chrome, and the median label was right-aligned at the frame edge, printing straight through this week's value label: `USUA…3.9H…H`. It now sits at the left over a stock white-out, painted in front of the columns while the rule stays behind them, so a tall week neither slices the label nor gets sliced by the rule. Pinned with a regression test at `test/app/form-guide.test.ts`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean on both tsconfigs
- **427 tests pass, 40 new** (baseline was 387)
- Coverage **99.6% statements / 97.4% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines** against the repo's 95% gate
- Rendered and eyeballed in **both themes** in headless Chrome

Two honesty notes: the preview rewrites tile URLs to CARTO because a `file://` page has no Worker to proxy them, and I put em dashes in four new comments before catching it against your standing rule and stripping them.

## The checkpoint

`01M0GFTSN16MMT2Q31ZDFYRHCW` on `380361d`, pushed and indexed, summary generated. Its `explain` now opens with Intent, Outcome and Learnings across Repository / Code / Workflow, including that the preview screenshot is what caught the collision.

The trail is done, and it merged while I was working on it.

## What "trail" was, and my miss

`entire trail` is a real command group. It appears in **neither** `entire --help` nor `entire labs --help`, which is why I read "trail" as a typo and burned a turn asking instead of just running `entire trail --help`. I've saved that so it doesn't happen again.

## The mismatch I found

Trail #1 was titled "form guide under map, scale bar" but its branch couldn't hold that work:

- The branch was cut from **main** (`31cef90`)
- **main had never carried the basemap.** The map, the scale bar and the form guide all lived on `feat/route-basemap`, which diverged at `f928eb8`
- main had since gained 7 commits `feat/route-basemap` never saw: Entire credit line, results table, route glyphs, `/catalogue`, mood media

Your `trail resume` also failed for two separate reasons: the checkpoint it wanted was back at `e93ce40` with 5 newer commits lacking checkpoints, and the confirmation prompt needs a TTY (`bubbletea: could not open TTY`). It had already switched the working branch before dying.

## What I did

Merged `feat/route-basemap` into the trail branch so it contains the work its title describes. Five conflicts:

| File | Call |
|---|---|
| `wrangler.jsonc` | Kept main's **production** `REDIRECT_URI` plus `BASEMAP=on`. The feature branch still pointed at `localhost:8787`, which an earlier session had flagged as something that would break Strava reconnect. |
| `src/app/render.ts` | Kept main's results table, took the feature branch's 3-arg `receipts(snapshot, nowMs, tz)` that the shared body needs for the timezone-aware `agoLabel`. Page order: map → form guide → receipts → results. |
| `src/app/styles.ts`, `src/domain/facts.ts` | Both sides added, both kept. |
| `.entire/settings.json` | Took the superset. |

Also folded the chart's `MONTH_ABBR` into main's existing `MONTHS`. The merge had pulled two copies of the same twelve strings into one file.

## Verification

- **453 tests pass** (22 files), typecheck clean on both tsconfigs
- Coverage **99.4% statements / 96.8% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines** against the 95% gate
- Screenshotted the merged page: map, form guide and results table coexisting in the right order

## It's on main now

While I was verifying, the trail merged as **PR #2**. `main` is now `188f553`, and its tree is **byte-identical** to the `b7aaac2` tree I verified, so that verification applies to main exactly as it stands. Trail #1 reads `status: merged`, `type: feature`, and its phase advanced `planning → building` when I pushed.

<https://entire.io/gh/elizabethsiegle/tedlasso-strava/trails/1>

## One thing I couldn't do

I could not set the trail's description. `--body` is rejected by the PATCH route, and the documented `PUT .../trails/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/{n}/body` returns a bare 422 for every payload shape I tried. The body is a collaboratively-synced document (`bodyDocument.contentJson`, with a `documentKey` and `schemaVersion`), not a simple string, and there's no published request schema. I stopped rather than keep guessing at an internal endpoint. I have the description written and ready if you want to paste it into the web UI, or you can tell me the expected shape.

## Three things stood between you and a running server

**1. The command.** `wrangler` isn't an npm subcommand. The script is `dev`:

```bash
npm run dev
```

**2. But `npm run dev` fails on this repo right now.** Pre-existing, nothing to do with the trail work:

```
✘ This Worker requires compatibility date "2026-08-14",
  but the newest date supported by this server binary is "2026-07-08".
```

`wrangler.jsonc` asks for `2026-08-14` while the pinned wrangler 4.107.0 ships a workerd that tops out at `2026-07-08`. This is the same mismatch the test suite has been warning about all along (it falls back silently there, but `wrangler dev` refuses to start). What actually works:

```bash
npx wrangler dev --test-scheduled --compatibility-date=2026-07-08
```

**3. Missing local config and data.** I created `.dev.vars` from `.dev.vars.example` (gitignored) so the server would boot, and seeded the local KV so the page has something to draw:

```bash
npx wrangler kv key put "snapshot/current" --binding STORE --local --path snapshot.json
```

Without that seed the page correctly shows its first-run empty state, "The first fetch hasn't run yet," and none of the figures render.

## Two caveats on what you're looking at

The `.dev.vars` values are **placeholders**, so `/auth/login` and `/api/refresh` won't work locally. And the snapshot I seeded is **synthetic** (a 9.4 km Panhandle-to-Golden-Gate-Park loop, twelve invented weeks peaking at 6.2 h), not your real Strava data. It's there to exercise the renderer.

## The compat-date fix, your call

I didn't change this since it's outside "run dev," but it's worth fixing so `npm run dev` just works:

- **Upgrade wrangler** (it suggests 4.125.0 itself). Cleaner, keeps the newer compat date, but bumps the runtime under your tests.
- **Lower `compatibility_date` to `2026-07-08`** in `wrangler.jsonc`. One line, minimal risk, works with the pinned wrangler.

content.text:
Now I have the semantic map, and Machiavelli maps onto it well:

| slot | condition | Machiavelli angle |
|---|---|---|
| `preseason` | no activity at all | fortune favours the prepared; peacetime is for building |
| `whered-you-go` | dormant 10+ days | states decay when neglected |
| `believe` | fresh 90-day best | seize the moment (*occasione*) |
| `roy-kent` | 5+ day streak | discipline sustained |
| `comeback-szn` | back after a layoff | recovering a lost state |
| `diamond-dogs` / `football-is-life` / `gaffer-mode` / `hopeful` / `biscuits` | the score grid | virtù vs fortuna in its various mixes |

Three things I'll hold to regardless of scope: **only genuinely citable passages** with chapter references (Machiavelli is one of the most misquoted authors there is; "the ends justify the means" appears nowhere in *The Prince*), the `character` field becoming a real citation like `The Prince, ch. XXV`, and the existing `verifiedOn` discipline.

Two scope calls are genuinely yours, though, because they change the size of this a lot.

feat: pivot the catalogue from Ted Lasso to Machiavelli

All 31 quotes replaced with 30 cited passages, and the ten moods renamed:
Peacetime, Neglect, Occasione, Discipline, Reconquest, The Middle Way,
Virtu, The Fortress, Fortuna, Ozio. The names now map onto what each slot
actually means: Peacetime is the no-activity state (ch. XIV, prepare in
peace), Neglect is dormancy (ch. VII, things that rise fast have no roots),
Occasione is a fresh 90-day best (ch. VI, opportunity and the powers to use
it), Ozio is idleness (ch. XXIV, blame not fortune but your own indolence).

What deliberately did NOT change:

- The mood ids. preseason, roy-kent, biscuits and the rest are engine keys,
  and CLAUDE.md treats the mood engine's fixture tests as ground truth.
  Renaming them would churn safety-critical code for a content change, so
  only Mood.name moved. The ids stay visible in ?preview= URLs; accepted.
- The accents. All ten were contrast-checked to 3:1 against both stocks in
  an earlier pass, so reusing them keeps that verification valid.
- Quote.character's field name. It holds a citation now ("The Prince, ch.
  XXV") rather than a speaker, but snapshots already in KV store
  quote.character and renaming it would orphan every one of them.

On accuracy: Machiavelli is one of the most misquoted authors there is, so
every entry is a passage that can be pointed at in the text, cited by
chapter, rendered from the public-domain translations. The popular
fabrications are deliberately absent; "the ends justify the means" appears
nowhere in The Prince and is not in this file.

Media: the 17 Giphy clips are gone. Each mood carries one public-domain
still from Wikimedia Commons, every URL confirmed to return 200 image/jpeg:
portraits by Santi di Tito and Crespi Castoldi, engravings after Ussi and by
Mentzel, Faruffini's Borgia and Machiavelli, Agneni's shades of the
Florentines, the Principe title page, and a caricature for Ozio. A
Renaissance oil printed on newsprint suits this sheet better than a reaction
GIF did.

The empty state changed register but not its rule: "Quiet on the pitch...
the door's open" became "Ninety days quiet... Fortune has had the whole of
it. The other half is yours whenever you want it back." Drier, still not a
telling-off. The football framing elsewhere is kept on purpose, because a
Renaissance strategist's matchday programme is the joke, not an oversight.

Two render tests now read the mood name from the catalogue instead of
hardcoding it, so the next rename does not fail them.

Verified: 460 tests pass, typecheck clean on both tsconfigs, coverage 99.4%
statements / 96.9% branches against the 95% gate, all ten image URLs checked
live, and the page served from wrangler dev and screenshotted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
echo "exit $?"; git log --oneline -1; git push -q -u origin feat/machiavelli-catalogue 2>&1 | tail -3; echo pushed

content.text:
Pivoted, and it suits the sheet better than I expected.

## The ten moods, renamed to what the slots actually mean

| id (unchanged) | condition | new name | anchor passage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preseason` | no activity at all | **Peacetime** | ch. XIV, prepare in peace |
| `whered-you-go` | dormant 10+ days | **Neglect** | ch. VII, things that rise fast have no roots |
| `believe` | fresh 90-day best | **Occasione** | ch. VI, opportunity and the powers to use it |
| `roy-kent` | 5+ day streak | **Discipline** | ch. XVIII, the fox and the lion |
| `comeback-szn` | back after a layoff | **Reconquest** | ch. III, provinces recovered are less apt to be lost again |
| `diamond-dogs` | both scores mid | **The Middle Way** | *Discourses* II.23, never adopt a middle course |
| `football-is-life` | both scores high | **Virtù** | ch. VI, own ability keeps what it wins |
| `gaffer-mode` | high consistency | **The Fortress** | ch. XX, the best fortress is not being hated |
| `hopeful` | high charge | **Fortuna** | ch. XXV, arbiter of half our actions |
| `biscuits` | both low | **Ozio** | ch. XXIV, blame not fortune but your own indolence |

## Three things I deliberately left alone

**The ids.** They're engine keys, and your `CLAUDE.md` treats the mood engine's fixture tests as ground truth. Renaming them would churn safety-critical code for a content change. Only `Mood.name` moved, which is the sole reader-facing label.

**The accents.** All ten were contrast-checked to 3:1 against both stocks in an earlier pass. Reusing them keeps that verification valid rather than silently invalidating it.

**`Quote.character`'s field name.** It holds `The Prince, ch. XXV` now instead of a speaker, but snapshots already in KV store `quote.character`, so renaming would orphan every one of them.

## On accuracy, which mattered here

Machiavelli is one of the most misquoted authors there is, so every one of the 30 entries is a passage that can be pointed at in the text, cited by chapter, from the public-domain translations. **"The ends justify the means" appears nowhere in *The Prince*** and is not in this file. I added that rule to `CLAUDE.md` so it survives the next session.

## Media

The 17 Giphy clips are gone. Each mood now carries one public-domain still from Wikimedia Commons, and I confirmed all ten return `200 image/jpeg` before writing any of them in. The screenshot shows Santi di Tito's portrait beside ch. XIV, and a Renaissance oil printed on newsprint stock genuinely reads better than a reaction GIF ever did.

I also changed the empty state's register while keeping its rule: "Quiet on the pitch, the door's open" became "Ninety days quiet. Fortune has had the whole of it. The other half is yours whenever you want it back." Drier, still not a telling-off. I kept the football framing elsewhere on purpose, because a Renaissance strategist's matchday programme is the joke rather than an oversight. Say the word if you'd rather that went too.

## Verification

460 tests pass, typecheck clean on both tsconfigs, coverage 99.4% statements / 96.9% branches against the 95% gate, and the page served from `wrangler dev` and screenshotted. Two render tests now read the mood name from the catalogue instead of hardcoding it, so the next rename won't fail them.

Pushed as `feat/machiavelli-catalogue` (`8606ece`). The dev server is still up on :8787 if you want to click around.

**One thing worth your attention:** those ten images are fetched by the visitor's browser straight from `upload.wikimedia.org`. That's the same shape of leak your basemap decision refuses for tiles, where everything goes through `/tiles/` so the provider sees one Worker instead of every visitor. The Giphy URLs had the identical problem before today, so it's not a regression, but the tile proxy is the established pattern and media should probably follow it. Want me to add a `/media/` proxy?
